title: Best Bath Towels UK
short: Egyptian cotton and everyday bath towels compared by GSM, absorbency and price, from budget to luxury.
intro: A towel's GSM (grams per square metre) is the single biggest clue to how thick, absorbent and long-lasting it will be, though material and weave matter too. This guide compares towels tested by Ideal Home's team, from affordable everyday sets to luxury Egyptian cotton.

guide.q: What GSM should I look for in a bath towel?
guide.a: GSM (grams per square metre) is a rough guide to thickness and absorbency. Around 400-500gsm suits a lighter, quicker-drying towel. 500-700gsm gives a thicker, more absorbent, hotel-style feel, though it also takes longer to dry.

Egyptian cotton has longer fibres, which generally makes for a softer, more durable towel that holds up better over repeated washes. Regular cotton towels can still perform well, especially at higher GSM, but tend to feel coarser sooner.

guide.q: How do I keep towels soft and absorbent?
guide.a: Avoid fabric softener, which coats the fibres and reduces absorbency over time. Wash new towels before first use to remove manufacturing residues, and tumble dry on a low heat or line dry to help maintain fluffiness.

guide.q: How often should I replace bath towels?
guide.a: Well-made towels can last several years with good care. Replace them once they feel thin, stop absorbing water well, or develop a persistent musty smell that washing doesn't fix.
